Details A curve with three parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane on the grid lines. The x axis is displayed from negative 7 to 8 in increments of 1 unit. The y axis is displayed from negative 4 to 4 in increments of 1 unit. The first part enters at approximately (negative 7, 1.9), goes down and to the right, concave down, crosses the x axis at approximately (negative 3.2, 0), concave up, reaches a low point at approximately (negative 1.5, negative 1.2), goes up and to the right through the origin, and exits the top of the viewing window in the first quadrant to the left of x = 1. The second part enters the viewing window at the top of the first quadrant to the right of x = 1, goes down and to the right, concave up, then becomes concave down after crossing the x axis, continues to go down and to the right in the fourth quadrant and exits very close to the left of x = 3. The third part enters the fourth quadrant from the bottom very close to x = 3, goes up and to the right through the point (4, negative 1), concave down, reaches a high point in the fourth quadrant, then goes down and to the right, concave up, approaching y = negative 2, and exits the viewing window at approximately (8, negative 1.9).

The equations of the asymptotes Details A function with three parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane on the grid lines. The x axis is displayed from negative 7 to 8 in increments of 1 unit. The y axis is displayed from negative 4 to 4 in increments of 1 unit. The first part enters the third quadrant at approximately (negative 7, negative 1.1), runs rightward with few ups and downs until x = negative 3, then goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches a high point at approximately (negative 1, 0.2), then falls steeply to the right in the fourth quadrant, exiting to the left of the y axis. The second part of the function resembles an inverted U-shape curve. It enters from the bottom of the fourth quadrant, very close to the y axis, goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches a high point in the first quadrant at approximately (1.2, 0.5), goes down and to the right in the fourth quadrant, exiting very close to and to the left of x = 2. The third part enters the first quadrant very close to and to the right of x = 2, goes down and to the right, concave up, reaches a low point at approximately (2, 1.1), rises to (5, 2.2), and falls to (6, 1.8), then rises and falls as the curve proceeds rightward, exiting the viewing window at (8, 1.9).

problem.paragraph: End Behavior of a Function By the end behavior of a function we mean the behavior of its values as $$\left. x\rightarrow\infty \right.$$ and as $$\left. x\rightarrow - \infty \right.$$ .

list.item: Describe and compare the end behavior of the functions $${P{(x)} = 3x^{5} - 5x^{3} + 2x} {Q{(x)} = 3x^{5}}$$ by graphing both functions in the viewing rectangles $$\left\lbrack {- 2,2} \right\rbrack$$ by $$\left\lbrack {- 2,2} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\left\lbrack {- 10,10} \right\rbrack$$ by $$\left\lbrack {- 10,000,10,000} \right\rbrack$$ .
Two functions are said to have the same end behavior if their ratio approaches $$1$$ as $$\left. x\rightarrow\infty \right.$$ . Show that $$P$$ and $$Q$$ have the same end behavior.

A tank contains $$5000L$$ of pure water. Brine that contains $$30$$ g of salt per liter of water is pumped into the tank at a rate of $$25L \slash \min$$ . Show that the concentration of salt after $$t$$ minutes (in grams per liter) is $$C(t) = \frac{30t}{200 + t}$$
What happens to the concentration as $$\left. t\rightarrow\infty \right.$$ ?
